title: Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with Large Language Models
layout_note: The two stacked prompt rows sit to the right of a search tree that feeds them; the stacked rows are the module, the tree on the left is the context they act on.
grouping: A search tree on the left and two stacked rows on the right - (a) Propose Prompt -> LM -> Thought Generation, and (b) Value Prompt -> LM -> Thought Evaluation. The tree's first level is enclosed in a grey dashed box joined by a thick grey arrow to row (a); one node is enclosed in an orange dashed box joined by a thick orange arrow to row (b).
shapes_depth: Prompt and output panels are rounded rectangles with a title bar in bold monospace (grey title for generation, cream-orange title for evaluation) and body text in a sans face, with italic grey placeholders ({one example}, {more examples}, {...more lines...}) standing for elided prompt text; key numbers are shaded grey or pink, the verdict 'impossible' pink. The LM is a plain white rounded box with bold monospace 'LM'. Tree nodes are bare arithmetic steps without boxes, green for kept and red for dead-end, each with a small '(left: ...)' remainder underneath; thin grey branch lines.
proposed_highlight: Colour ties the two halves: the grey dashed selection and arrow lead to the generation row with its grey titles, the orange ones to the evaluation row with its orange titles.
lesson: Tie each highlighted part of a search tree to the prompt row that produces or judges it with a matching coloured dashed box and arrow, so the tree and the prompt templates explain each other.
notes: Venue and year from the PDF's first page (NeurIPS 2023). Carded under llm-agents as an LLM deliberate-search method; elements 'other' = the verbatim prompt/output text panels.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

taxonomy.task: Game of 24 reasoning with LM-generated and LM-evaluated thoughts

core.what: a Game-of-24 search tree on the left (Input: 4 9 10 13 at the root, arithmetic thoughts with their remaining numbers as nodes) has two nodes boxed by dashed outlines - grey around the root, orange around a '4+9=13' child - and a thick arrow from each box points to the prompt row that is applied to that node

relations.form: the tree is drawn three levels deep with real thoughts ('10-4=6 (left: 6 9 13)', '4*6=24 (left: 24)'), green nodes for promising and red for failing ones, '......' for elided branches
a grey dashed box around the root sends a thick grey arrow right to the (a) Propose Prompt row; an orange dashed box around one child sends a thick orange arrow down-right to the (b) Value Prompt row
each of two rows reads left to right: a prompt card with its literal text -> an 'LM' box -> an output card (Thought Generation with candidate steps; Thought Evaluation ending in 'impossible')
the two rows are stacked with their LM boxes aligned one above the other, the same model used for proposing and for valuing

channels.colour: in the tree green = viable thought, red = failing thought; grey vs orange = generation vs evaluation (dashed box, arrow, card header); pink highlight = the node's numbers being judged and the verdict, grey highlight = the chosen generated thought - several tints but each with one job; the green/red code is not keyed
channels.shape: plain text nodes = tree states; cards with monospaced headers = prompts and outputs; rounded square = LM
channels.line: thin grey arrows = tree edges and data flow; thick grey/orange arrows = which node a prompt is applied to
channels.frame: dashed outlines = the node selected for a prompt

quality.strengths: the method acts on a structure and the figure draws that structure as a small real instance, with the node each prompt reads boxed and colour-matched to its row (grey = propose, orange = value); prompts and outputs are quoted literally, including the few-shot placeholders and the 'impossible' verdict, so the reader sees exactly what the LM is given and returns
quality.weaknesses: the two LM boxes are separate copies whose sameness rests on the label; the green/red node colours are unkeyed; how the evaluation result feeds back to prune or expand the tree is not drawn, so the search loop is implied rather than shown; the orange arrow crosses diagonally from the tree's middle into the lower row

insights.structure: A search tree on the left feeds two stacked rows on the right, (a) Propose Prompt -> LM -> Thought Generation and (b) Value Prompt -> LM -> Thought Evaluation, with the same three-column alignment in both rows.
insights.data: Prompts and outputs are panels with a monospace title bar and real prompt text, italic grey placeholders ({one example}, {...more lines...}) for elided parts; tree nodes are bare arithmetic steps coloured green (kept) or red (dead end) with a small '(left: ...)' remainder.
insights.emphasis: Colour links context to module: a grey dashed box around the tree's first level and a grey arrow go to row (a), an orange dashed box around one node and an orange arrow go to row (b), whose title bars are cream-orange.
insights.flow: Left to right: tree -> thick coloured arrows -> prompt panel -> LM box -> output panel; the tree itself reads top to bottom.
insights.avoid: The tree's lower levels have no link back from Thought Evaluation, so how the value verdict prunes the tree is left to the colours alone.

arrangement.units: two unframed horizontal rows (a) generation and (b) evaluation, each prompt panel -> LM -> output panel, plus an unframed tree column at left
arrangement.inputs_as: the search tree with real arithmetic nodes; 'Input: 4 9 10 13' at its top
arrangement.shared: the LM box is drawn once per row
